title: Pulsed Field or Cryoballoon Pulmonary Vein Isolation for Atrial Fibrillation in Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) frequently coexist, worsening prognosis. While catheter ablation confers clinical benefits in this high-risk population, comparative data between novel non-thermal pulsed field ablation (PFA) and established cryoballoon ablation (CBA) for AF-therapy in patients with HFrEF are limited. OBJECTIVE: To compare the efficacy and safety of PFA- with CBA-based pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) in patients with AF and HFrEF (left ventricular ejection fraction ≤40%). METHODS: This retrospective, international multicenter study included patients with HFrEF undergoing first-time PVI-only procedures between 2018 and 2025. Propensity-score matching (1:1 ratio) was applied to balance baseline characteristics. The primary efficacy endpoint was the first recurrence of any atrial tachyarrhythmia after a 3-month blanking period. Secondary measures included safety events and procedural efficiency. RESULTS: A total of 700 patients from 12 German and Canadian centers were included, with 420 patients analyzed following propensity-score matching. At 12 months, freedom from atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence with PFA was comparable to CBA (Kaplan-Meier estimates, 65.0% vs. 67.8%; hazard ratio, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.77 to 1.55; P=0.61). No statistically significant differences in observed safety outcomes were detected. PFA significantly improved procedural efficiency with shorter total procedure duration (58±22min vs. 72±22min; P<0.001), left-atrial dwell time (42±16min vs. 52±17min; P<0.001) and lower contrast dye use (0 ml [IQR 0-15] vs. 47 ml [IQR 30-56], P<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: In patients with AF and HFrEF, PFA-based PVI achieves similar rhythm-control efficacy and safety compared with CBA, while significantly enhancing procedural efficiency.

title: Racial and Ethnic Disparities in Postarrest Cardiac Procedures for Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Effective postarrest care facilitates optimal outcomes for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Relatively little research has evaluated whether there may be racial or ethnic disparities in the workup and management of the patient post arrest. METHODS: We retrospectively studied out-of-hospital cardiac arrests using the TriNetX research database. We defined out-of-hospital cardiac arrest as any emergency department visit (2013-2024) with a diagnosis of cardiac arrest and included patients who survived to admission. Multivariate adjusted logistic regression was used to compare rates of the following cardiac interventions across race or ethnicity: (1) echocardiography; (2) left heart catheterization; (3) percutaneous coronary intervention; (4) ventricular assist device placement; and (5) automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement. RESULTS: A total of 58 394 cases of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest met inclusion criteria. Compared with White patients (left heart catheterization: 13.9%, percutaneous coronary intervention: 7.1%, ventricular assist device: 3.0%, automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator: 0.9%), Black patients had lower odds of receiving left heart catheterization (7.2%, adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.60 [95% CI, 0.55-0.64]), percutaneous coronary intervention (2.6%, aOR, 0.47 [95% CI, 0.42-0.53]), ventricular assist device placement (1.6%, aOR, 0.70 [95% CI, 0.60-0.80]), and automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement (0.4%, aOR, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.41-0.70]). Hispanic/Latino patients were also less likely to receive left heart catheterization (8.9%, aOR, 0.72 [95% CI, 0.64-0.80]), percutaneous coronary intervention (3.7%, aOR, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.53-0.74]), and automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement (0.4%, aOR, 0.52 [95% CI, 0.33-0.81]). CONCLUSIONS: Our large multicenter analysis identifies racial or ethnic disparities in postarrest cardiac workup and management. Further research is needed to identify potential causes for these disparities with the hope of developing strategies to address them.

title: Myocardial Responses to Eplontersen in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: The CARDIO-TTRansform CMR study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Transthyretin-lowering therapies target the underlying cause of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), but their effects on myocardial amyloid burden and cardiac remodelling remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated the myocardial effects of sustained transthyretin suppression with eplontersen using serial multiparametric cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR). METHODS: This CMR study was a pre-specified, international, prospective study embedded within the randomized, placebo-controlled phase 3 CARDIO-TTRansform trial. Participants underwent CMR at baseline and planned assessments at weeks 25, 49, 97, and 140. The primary imaging analysis evaluated longitudinal changes in CMR parameters using mixed models for repeated measures. Myocardial amyloid regression and progression were defined as ≥5 percentage-point decreases and increases in extracellular volume (ECV), respectively. All other patients were considered stable. RESULTS: We enrolled 120 participants with baseline and ≥1 follow-up CMR assessment (eplontersen, n=58; placebo, n=62; mean age, 76.7±6.5 years; 95% male; baseline stabilizer, 12.5%). At week 140 eplontersen resulted in lower ECV, compared with placebo (least-squares mean difference [95% CI], -6.7 percentage points [ -8.7 to -4.7]; P<0.001) and lower native T1 ( -25.9ms [-41.7 to -10.2 ]; P=0.002) and left ventricular mass (-19.1g [-28.0 to -10.2]; P<0.001). Eplontersen also increased left ventricular ejection fraction (+5.1% [1.8-8.3]; P=0.002), right ventricular ejection fraction (+4.6% [0.6-8.7]; P=0.03), and left ventricular global longitudinal, circumferential, and radial strain and right ventricular longitudinal strain (all P<0.05), compared to placebo. At week-140, myocardial amyloid regression occurred in 12.5% receiving eplontersen versus 0% receiving placebo, whereas progression occurred in 12.5% versus 76%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Sustained transthyretin suppression with eplontersen resulted in substantially lower myocardial ECV and favorable changes in cardiac structure, biventricular systolic function, and myocardial deformation compared with placebo in a cohort of patients mostly not on background stabilizer at baseline. These findings provide randomized evidence that lowering circulating transthyretin modifies myocardial disease progression in ATTR-CM and support serial multiparametric CMR for characterizing myocardial treatment response.

title: Impact of Coronary Sinus Reducer on the Extent of Ischemia in Functional Stress Tests.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The coronary sinus reducer is an established therapy for patients with refractory angina due to obstructive coronary artery disease who are not candidates for further revascularization. Although symptomatic benefits are well documented, its effect on objective measures of ischemia remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between coronary sinus reducer implantation and inducible myocardial ischemia assessed by functional stress testing. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed a prospectively maintained registry of consecutive patients undergoing coronary sinus reducer implantation between 2011 and 2024. Baseline assessment included Canadian Cardiovascular Society angina class, 6-minute walk test, stress echocardiography, and dipyridamole single-photon emission computed tomography imaging, repeated at 6 months. Coprimary outcomes were changes in stress wall motion score index and in the proportion of patients with moderate or severe ischemia on single-photon emission computed tomography. Clinical nonresponders were defined as no improvement in Canadian Cardiovascular Society class at 12 months. RESULTS: Among 153 treated patients, 118 had complete imaging data. Median stress wall motion score index improved from 1.38 to 1.23 (P<0.001), and stress left ventricular ejection fraction increased from 55% to 60% (P=0.019). The proportion of patients with moderate or severe ischemia on single-photon emission computed tomography decreased from 52% to 24% (P<0.001). The summed difference score, available in 45 patients, did not change significantly. Clinically, 86% improved by ≥1 Canadian Cardiovascular Society class at 6 months. CONCLUSIONS: Coronary sinus reducer implantation was associated with reduced inducible ischemia on stress echocardiography and with clinical improvement. The proportion of patients with moderate or severe ischemia on single-photon emission computed tomography decreased following Reducer implantation.

title: Tricuspid inflow E-wave velocity for the assessment of severe or greater tricuspid regurgitation: derivation and external validation of threshold values.
abstract: AIMS: Current guidelines include tricuspid inflow E-wave (>100 cm/s by pulsed-wave Doppler) as a semiquantitative criterion for diagnosing severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR), despite limited supporting evidence. We assessed its diagnostic performance for identifying severe or greater TR, deriving and externally validating practical thresholds. METHODS AND RESULTS: Tricuspid inflow E-wave velocity was measured by pulsed-wave Doppler in consecutive patients with at least mild TR between December 2024 and February 2026. Among 178 patients (77±13 years, 65% women), TR was mild in 44, moderate in 61, severe in 44, massive in 15, and torrential in 14. Mean tricuspid E-wave velocity was 56±16 cm/s and increased with TR severity: 47±8, 50±10, 62±16, 67±13, and 77±21 cm/s for mild, moderate, severe, massive, and torrential TR. Only three patients had E-wave velocity >100 cm/s (one with severe and two with torrential TR). Using multiparametric echocardiographic grading as the reference standard, the >100 cm/s threshold showed 5.5% sensitivity, 100% specificity, and kappa 0.25 for severe or greater TR. As a continuous variable, E-wave velocity discriminated severe or greater TR with an AUC of 0.81. A lower threshold of 52 cm/s yielded 81% sensitivity and 67% specificity, whereas 47 cm/s provided 90% sensitivity and 43% specificity. External validation resulted in 94% sensitivity and 47% specificity. CONCLUSION: The guideline-recommended threshold of >100 cm/s is highly insensitive for detecting severe or greater TR. Lower cut-offs, particularly 47 cm/s, may be useful for screening to trigger a comprehensive multiparametric assessment.

title: Effect of two common GVHD prophylaxis regimens on the gut microbiome in a randomized phase 3 trial.
abstract: Allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation can cure certain hematological disorders but has many complications. In retrospective studies, low gut microbiome diversity is associated with adverse clinical outcomes. In 2023, the Blood and Marrow Transplant Clinical Trials Network 1703 randomized phase 3 trial demonstrated the superiority of post-transplant cyclophosphamide (PTCy) and mycophenolate mofetil to tacrolimus and methotrexate (Tac/MTX) for graft-versus-host disease prophylaxis in participants with hematological malignancies undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation. Here we report on the microbiome-focused companion study to 1703, Blood and Marrow Transplant Clinical Trials Network 1801, which coenrolled participants and shared trial registration. The primary endpoint was association between microbiome diversity at neutrophil engraftment and non-relapse mortality after 1 year; secondary endpoints included associations with other clinical outcomes and with baseline microbiome diversity. Based on 2575 longitudinally collected stool samples from 304 participants (Tac/MTX n = 147, PTCy n = 157), no association between engraftment microbiome diversity and non-relapse mortality was observed (P = 0.314), not meeting the primary endpoint. Lower baseline microbiome diversity was associated with shorter overall survival (P = 0.007). Safety data were reported in the original 1703 publication. In exploratory analyses, microbiome diversity and absolute microbial load were lower in PTCy compared to Tac/MTX on days 14-28 following HCT, independent of non-prophylaxis antibiotics exposure. Microbial domination events, when a single species exceeds 30% relative abundance, did not differ significantly between study arms and reflected both pathogen blooms and less severe disruptions of the microbial community. Clostridium scindens and secondary bile-acid metabolism pathways were less prevalent in PTCy than in Tac/MTX following HCT. In summary, we find prophylaxis regimens likely exert independent effects on both the microbiome and immune compartments and can also impact their interaction. Understanding whether and how microbiome-targeted interventions might improve transplant outcomes will therefore require careful disentangling of these effects within each specific treatment context. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03959241 .

title: Population Impact of the 2026 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Dyslipidemia Guideline on Lipid-Lowering Therapy Eligibility Among US Adults.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The 2026 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association dyslipidemia guideline replaces the pooled cohort equations with the atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease component of the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events equations for primary prevention risk estimation and modifies lipid-lowering therapy (LLT) eligibility by lowering the risk-based treatment threshold and expanding diabetes and chronic kidney disease criteria. The population-level impact of this transition is uncertain. METHODS: We analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2021 to 2023 participants aged 40 to 75 years without self-reported atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and with available low-density lipoprotein cholesterol. Survey weights were used to generate national estimates. Guideline-supported LLT eligibility was assessed under the 2018 pooled cohort equations-based American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association cholesterol framework and the 2026 Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events-based American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association dyslipidemia framework. Current LLT use was assessed among guideline-supported adults. RESULTS: The analytic sample included 1662 participants, representing 115.05 million US adults. LLT was supported for 42.82 million adults under the 2018 framework and 42.17 million under the 2026 framework, a net decrease of 0.65 million. Reclassification was substantial: 37.42 million remained supported, 5.40 million lost support, 4.75 million newly gained support, and 67.48 million remained unsupported. Among supported adults, current LLT use was 39.4% under the 2018 framework and 40.5% under the 2026 framework. CONCLUSIONS: Transition to the 2026 Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events-based framework produced little net change in LLT eligibility but meaningfully changed who was supported for therapy. Persistent undertreatment remains a major implementation gap.

title: zG CreERT2 Uncovers Migration and Sex-Dependent NPC1 in Aldosterone Synthesis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The adrenal zona glomerulosa (zG) is the primary site of aldosterone synthesis. Inducible genetic tools are important for investigating zG cell function and fate in adult mice. This study aimed to generate and validate a tamoxifen-inducible, zG-specific aldosterone synthase-CreERT2 mouse model and investigate the zG-specific role of NPC1 (Niemann-Pick type C1) in aldosterone synthesis. METHODS: Aldosterone synthase-CreERT2 mice were generated by clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats/clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeat-associated 9 knock-in of P2A (porcine teschovirus-1 2A peptide)-CreERT2 into the Cyp11b2 locus. Cre specificity and efficiency were validated by quantitative polymerase chain reaction, immunofluorescence, and lineage tracing. The model was then used to conditionally delete Npc1 in the zG. RESULTS: Cre expression and activity were confined to the zG. Heterozygous aldosterone synthase-CreERT2 mice showed normal adrenal morphology and hormone levels despite reduced Cyp11b2 expression. Homozygosity of the CreERT2 allele significantly reduced Cyp11b2 expression and aldosterone levels and increased renin in both sexes, indicating a gene-dosage effect. Lineage tracing confirmed the centripetal migration of zG cells to the zona fasciculata, which was faster in female mice. Strikingly, zG-specific Npc1 deletion reduced aldosterone in female mice under a normal-sodium diet, whereas increased renin and decreased aldosterone-to-renin ratio were observed in male mice under a high-sodium diet, indicating a sex-dependent effect. CONCLUSIONS: The aldosterone synthase-CreERT2 mouse provides a powerful and specific platform for spatiotemporally controlled dissection of zG biology, with the heterozygous line recommended for use to avoid Cre-associated dosage effects. Using this model, we identify a sex-dependent effect of zG-specific Npc1 deletion on aldosterone regulation, providing new insight into sex differences in adrenal physiology and aldosterone-related disorders.

title: Impact of the 2026 Dyslipidemia Guideline on ASCVD Reclassification and Statin Recommendations in MESA.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The 2026 American College of Cardiology (ACC)/American Heart Association (AHA)/Multisociety Guideline on the Management of Dyslipidemia recommends the use of the PREVENT (Predicting Risk of cardiovascular disease EVENTs) equations to predict atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk while concurrently revising previous risk-category thresholds. The impact of these reclassifications is yet to be described. OBJECTIVES: The authors characterized ASCVD reclassification and statin recommendations under the 2026 guideline, evaluated clinical events under this reclassification, and examined risk enhancement with risk enhancers and coronary artery calcium (CAC) burden. METHODS: Adults (N = 6,098) from the MESA (Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) were assessed, comparing the Pooled Cohort Equations (PCE) and 2013 thresholds to PREVENT with 2026 thresholds. We evaluated the degree of directional reclassification, impact on statin recommendations, and risk enhancement with biomarkers and CAC burden. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 10 years, 6.0% of participants had an ASCVD event. PREVENT reclassified 16.4% to a lower and 13.1% to a higher risk category as compared to the PCE. The statin recommendation under PREVENT was 50.4% compared to 55.2% under PCE. Of those who were no longer recommended for statin use, 4.9% went on to have an event. Individuals who were reclassified downward but had elevated CAC or any risk-enhancing factors had a higher event rate. CONCLUSIONS: Adherence to the 2026 guideline may lead to a small net downward reclassification of predicted ASCVD risk. Statin recommendations will fall modestly, however, not accompanied by a substantial number of subsequent events. Risk enhancers and elevated CAC identify higher risk subgroups than their PREVENT risk would suggest, emphasizing their supporting role in risk prediction.

title: Nonculprit Lesion Complexity and Timing of Complete Revascularization in Patients Presenting With Acute Coronary Syndrome and Multivessel Disease: Insights From the BIOVASC Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The optimal timing of complete revascularization for patients with acute coronary syndrome, multivessel disease and complex nonculprit coronary lesions (NCL) remains unclear. METHODS: The BIOVASC trial randomized patients with acute coronary syndrome and multivessel disease to immediate complete revascularization and staged complete revascularization. The primary end point was a composite of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, unplanned ischemia-driven revascularization, or cerebrovascular events at 2-year follow-up. In this exploratory post hoc analysis, patients were classified as having complex NCL if at least 1 nonculprit lesion met the following criteria: true bifurcation; severe calcification; lesion length >20 mm; aorto-ostial lesion; left main lesion. We aimed to compare a strategy of immediate complete revascularization and staged complete revascularization in patients presenting with acute coronary syndrome and multivessel disease with complex NCL. Moreover, we sought to compare patients with complex and noncomplex NCLs in terms of clinical outcomes. RESULTS: Among the 1525 patients enrolled in the BIOVASC trial, 550 (36.1%) had a complex NCL. The presence of a complex NCL was associated with a significantly higher incidence of the primary end point compared with noncomplex NCL (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.49 [95% CI, 1.11-2.02]; P=0.01), including spontaneous myocardial infarction (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.86 [95% CI, 1.12-3.09]; P=0.02). In patients with complex NCL, the cumulative incidence of the primary end point was 15.7% in the immediate complete revascularization group and 17.5% in the staged complete revascularization group (hazard ratio, 0.86 [95% CI, 0.57-1.31]; P=0.49). No significant interaction was observed between the presence of a complex NCL and revascularization strategy for the primary end point (P for interaction=0.40). CONCLUSIONS: In patients with acute coronary syndrome and multivessel disease, patients with complex NCL experienced worse clinical outcomes at 2-year follow-up, driven by higher rates of myocardial infarction. However, no statistically significant interaction was observed between NCL complexity and the effect of immediate complete revascularization versus staged complete revascularization. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT03621501.

title: Life Expectancy After Incident Ischemic Stroke in a Bi-Ethnic Population: Estimates Over 2005 to 2022.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study measured 5- and 10-year life expectancy after an incident ischemic stroke using a high-quality sample of Mexican Americans and non-Hispanic White patients over a recent period. METHODS: Data were from the Brain Attack Surveillance in Corpus Christi Project. The sample included 2011 Mexican American and 1262 non-Hispanic White men and women who had an incident ischemic stroke during 2005 to 2022 and were aged 45 years or older at the time of stroke. Participants were followed up to 18 years. Primary outcome was 5- and 10-year life expectancy. Discrete-time logistic regression models were implemented. RESULTS: Mean age at incident stroke was 69 years. There was no difference in the odds of dying between Mexican Americans and non-Hispanic White men and women after adjustment for age at stroke and sex. Among men, an incident stroke at age 70 years was associated with a 10-year life expectancy of 6.4 years (95% CI: 6.1-6.6) in Mexican Americans and 6.5 years (95% CI: 6.2-6.9) in non-Hispanic White adults. Among women, the analogous 10-year life expectancy was 6.7 years (95% CI: 6.3-6.8) in Mexican Americans and 6.8 years (95% CI: 6.4-7.0) in non-Hispanic White adults. Comparing these estimates to life expectancy at age 70 in the general US population indicates that stroke is associated with a life shortening effect of 2.1 to 2.4 years over 10 years. CONCLUSIONS: Life expectancy after an ischemic stroke did not differ between Mexican Americans and non-Hispanic White adults. Incident ischemic stroke remains associated with substantial life shortening effects in the recent period.

title: Effects of Eplontersen on Cardiac Structure and Function in Patients With Transthyretin Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy: Insights from the CARDIO-TTRansform Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In CARDIO-TTRansform, the TTR (transthyretin) silencer eplontersen did not significantly reduce the primary end point of cardiovascular death and recurrent cardiovascular events in patients with TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy, although treatment effects varied by baseline TTR stabilizer use. Whether eplontersen favorably affects cardiac structure and function is unknown. METHODS: CARDIO-TTRansform randomized 1432 patients with TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy to eplontersen (45 mg) subcutaneously every 4 weeks or placebo. Echocardiograms were performed at baseline and weeks 61, 97, and 140. Associations of baseline echocardiographic measures with all-cause mortality and the primary end point were evaluated using Cox and semiparametric proportional rates models. Between-group differences at week 140 were analyzed with mixed models for repeated measures. RESULTS: Among 1426 participants with baseline echocardiograms (mean age, 76±7 years, 91% men, 85% wild type, 57% receiving stabilizers), baseline measures of left ventricular systolic function (LV ejection fraction, global longitudinal strain, stroke volume, myocardial contraction fraction), diastolic function (E wave deceleration time, septal e', average E/e'), and right ventricular function and hemodynamics were independently associated with all-cause mortality or the primary end point. At week 140 (echocardiograms available in 554 patients in the eplontersen group and 506 in the placebo group), eplontersen attenuated increases in mean LV wall thickness (least-squares mean [LSM] difference, -0.24 mm [95% CI, -0.48 to -0.01]) and declines in LV stroke volume (LSM difference, 1.88 mL [95% CI, 0.07-3.69]), myocardial contraction fraction (LSM difference, 0.88% [95% CI, 0.25-1.57]), average E/e' (LSM difference, -0.71 [95% CI, -1.36 to -0.07]), and right ventricular outflow tract velocity-time integral (LSM difference, 0.42 [95% CI, 0.00-0.85]) versus placebo in the overall cohort. Beneficial effects were driven almost exclusively by patients not receiving stabilizers at baseline. No significant treatment effects were observed in patients receiving stabilizers. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy, eplontersen modestly attenuated deterioration in prognostically important measures of LV systolic, diastolic and right ventricular function, primarily among patients not receiving stabilizers at baseline. These findings complement the clinical findings of CARDIO-TTRansform and suggest that TTR silencing may attenuate progression of cardiac dysfunction in TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04136171; URL: xxx; Unique identifier: 2019-002835-27.

title: Case Volumes and Outcomes of Early-Career Operators Performing TAVR in the United States.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Operator experience is a key determinant of outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, whether early-career operators achieve comparable results to more experienced peers is unknown. Herein, we evaluate case volumes, patient risk profiles, and 30-day outcomes of early-career versus non-early-career operators performing TAVR in the United States. METHODS: Using the Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapies Registry, we identified isolated TAVR procedures from October 2011 through March 2024. Early-career status was defined as ≤5 years in independent practice (based on board certification or first TAVR date); non-early-career status was >5 years. Multivariable hierarchical models adjusted for patient-, procedural-, operator-, and site-level factors, including annualized institutional TAVR volume, while accounting for clustering of procedures within operators and operators within sites. Primary outcomes were 30-day mortality and a composite of death, stroke, major bleeding, stage III acute kidney injury, or moderate-to-severe paravalvular leak. RESULTS: A total of 634 723 TAVR procedures were performed by 3126 operators across 847 sites, including 90 376 (14.2%) by early-career operators. Median annualized lifetime volume was lower for early-career operators (13 [interquartile range, 5-31] versus 19 [interquartile range, 7-42] cases per year; P<0.001). After adjustment, 30-day mortality was similar between early-career and non-early-career operators (2.38% versus 2.44%; risk ratio, 0.97 [95% CI, 0.92-1.01]; P=0.293), whereas the composite end point was lower among early-career operators (11.19% versus 11.77%; risk ratio, 0.95 [95% CI, 0.93-0.98]; P<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: In a national TAVR registry, early-career operators performed fewer cases but achieved similar 30-day mortality and a modestly lower adjusted composite event rate relative to more experienced peers. These findings suggest that within the structured, team-based environment of contemporary TAVR programs, early-career status alone is not associated with inferior procedural outcomes and should not be viewed as a barrier to independent practice.

title: Age-Related Differences in Physical Activity for Primary Prevention of Coronary Heart Disease: Insights From Wearable Accelerometers.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Current physical activity recommendations suggest at least 150 minutes per week of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity for primary prevention of coronary heart disease (CHD) across ages. However, age-related disparities exist in exercise capability, engagement, and guideline adherence, and their implications for CHD prevention remain underexplored. METHODS: We included wrist-worn accelerometer data from 80 243 UK Biobank participants (aged 61.54±7.84 years, 57.3% women), classified as older (≥65 years; n=31 663) or middle-aged (<65 years; n=48 580). Cox proportional hazards models were applied to examine age-specific associations between physical activity and incident CHD. Nonlinear and dose-response relationships were assessed using restricted cubic splines, and age-related differences were tested using likelihood ratio tests. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 7.88 years, 3764 CHD events occurred. A 20% lower CHD risk (hazard ratio [HR], 0.8) was observed at approximately 60 minutes per week of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity in older adults versus 330 minutes per week in middle-aged adults (Pinteraction=0.006). Guideline adherence was associated with stronger inverse associations in older than in middle-aged adults (HR, 0.72 versus 0.85; Pinteraction=0.029). Older weekend warriors exhibited a 28% lower CHD risk, comparable with regularly active individuals, whereas the association was weaker and nonsignificant in middle-aged adults (Pinteraction=0.005). At 150 minutes per week, a 10% lower CHD risk corresponded to an acceleration threshold of 100 milligravity in middle-aged adults but approximately 55 milligravity in older adults. A possible U-shaped relationship was observed in older adults. CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest potential age-related heterogeneity in wearable-measured physical activity for CHD prevention, and may help motivate activity engagement among older adults and enhance CHD prevention.

title: Systemic Microvascular Endothelial Dysfunction in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction and Type 2 Diabetes: A Pooled Analysis of GLADIATOR-HFpEF, IRON-HFpEF, EMPA-MVD, Hoorn Diabetes Care System, and Healthy Controls.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is increasingly recognized as a systemic disorder featuring microvascular dysfunction and metabolic comorbidities such as type 2 diabetes (T2D). However, the extent to which systemic microvascular abnormalities reflect HFpEF or coexisting T2D remains incompletely understood. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to characterize systemic microvascular dysfunction in patients with HFpEF and to evaluate the contribution of comorbid T2D. METHODS: Systemic microvascular function, defined as flow responses expressed as cutaneous vascular conductance, was assessed using laser speckle contrast analysis with iontophoresis of acetylcholine, insulin, and sodium nitroprusside. Analysis adjusted for age and sex were performed across healthy controls (n = 23), T2D (n = 138), HFpEF without T2D (n = 63), and HFpEF with T2D (n = 27). RESULTS: Insulin-mediated microvascular perfusion was reduced in participants with T2D (-0.30 arbitrary perfusion units [APU]/mm Hg; P < 0.001) and in HFpEF with T2D (-0.32 APU/mm Hg; P = 0.004) compared with controls, whereas responses in HFpEF without T2D were not different from controls. Perfusion responses to sodium nitroprusside were reduced in T2D and HFpEF with T2D, while responses to acetylcholine were preserved. No statistically detectable interaction between HFpEF and T2D was observed. Sex did not modify the relationship between HFpEF and microvascular dysfunction, but exploratory sex-stratified analyses showed reduced insulin-mediated microvascular perfusion in T2D (mean difference: -0.30 APU/mm Hg; P = 0.020) and HFpEF + T2D (mean difference: -0.51 APU/mm Hg; P = 0.002) compared with controls. CONCLUSIONS: Systemic microvascular dysfunction, particularly impaired insulin-mediated vasodilation, was observed in HFpEF. The observed abnormalities were predominantly present in participants with comorbid type 2 diabetes.

title: First-in-Human Experience With a Novel Monorail Microcatheter for Instantaneous Coronary Pressure and Flow Velocity Measurements.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Invasive coronary physiology enables comprehensive assessment of epicardial and microvascular disease, but its routine use is limited by technical complexity and prolonged acquisition time. OBJECTIVES: The PyCath system is a rapid-exchange microcatheter engineered to simultaneously measure intracoronary pressure and thermoconvection-based flow velocity. METHODS: First-in-human, prospective, single-arm study evaluating the safety and performance of the PyCath system in patients with a clinical indication for coronary physiology assessment. The microcatheter was advanced over a standard coronary guidewire to acquire simultaneous pressure and flow velocity at baseline and during hyperemia. The primary objectives were procedural safety, defined as device-related major adverse cardiac events, and device performance, defined as successful acquisition of pressure and velocity signals. Data were analyzed by an independent core laboratory. RESULTS: Seventeen patients (mean age 59.3 ± 9.4 years, 76.5% males) referred for invasive coronary physiology assessment were included. Intracoronary pressure and velocity measurements were feasible in 100% and 88% of cases, respectively. The mean time required to obtain both measurements was 70.6 ± 23.6 seconds. The mean fractional flow reserve, coronary flow velocity reserve, and hyperemic microvascular resistance were 0.84 ± 0.12, 2.28 ± 0.79, and 1.46 ± 0.77, respectively. There were no device-related major adverse cardiac events. Test-retest reproducibility was good-to-excellent with intraclass correlation coefficients for fractional flow reserve, coronary flow velocity reserve, and hyperemic microvascular resistance of 0.979 (0.934-0.993), 0.798 (0.477-0.933), and 0.759 (0.397-0.919). CONCLUSIONS: In this first-in-human experience, the PyCath microcatheter enabled safe and reproducible measurements of intracoronary pressure and flow velocity with excellent reproducibility.

title: HOPO 14-1, an Oral Actinide Chelator: A Phase 1 Nonrandomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Current treatments approved by the US Food and Drug Administration for internal actinide contamination (pentetate calcium trisodium and pentetate zinc trisodium) require intravenous injection or nebulized inhalation under medical supervision and have limited radionuclide coverage. HOPO 14-1, an oral form of 3,4,3-LI(1,2-HOPO), is the first shelf-stable, broad-spectrum actinide chelator in clinical development that does not require intravenous access or trained personnel. In preclinical models, 3,4,3-LI(1,2-HOPO) removed a broad range of actinides, and its oral route supports scalable emergency medical use. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetic parameters, and excretion of a single dose of HOPO 14-1 in healthy adults. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a phase 1 nonrandomized clinical trial including 42 healthy adults (6 per dose level) with evaluations for 14 days after administration of a single dose and conducted at a single site in the US. Participants were recruited and screened between March 2023 and July 2025 and follow-up was completed in August 2025. INTERVENTION: Single oral dose of HOPO 14-1 administered at 1 of 7 dose levels (100 mg, 200 mg, 500 mg, 1200 mg, 2500 mg, 5000 mg, or 7500 mg) with follow-up through day 14 after dose administration. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcomes were the incidence and severity of adverse events, drug-related adverse events, and serious adverse events. The secondary outcomes were plasma pharmacokinetic parameters and cumulative urinary and fecal excretion. RESULTS: Of the 42 healthy adults enrolled (median age, 43 [IQR, 34-51] years; 64% female), all received a single dose of HOPO 14-1 (administered across all dose levels as assigned). There were no serious adverse events or dose-limiting toxic effects. The drug-related adverse events included diarrhea (31%), vomiting (14%), headache (12%), and fatigue (7%); all were mild to moderate in severity. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the principal tolerability findings and most evident at the highest doses. The plasma pharmacokinetic parameters demonstrated rapid absorption (median time of maximum plasma concentration, 0.86 [range, 0.53-1.60] hours to 1.90 [range, 1.40-2.90] hours) and dose-dependent increases in systemic exposure, with greater than proportional increases at higher doses. Fecal excretion was the primary route of elimination; urinary excretion was minimal. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Single oral doses of HOPO 14-1 up to 7500 mg were administered without dose-limiting toxicity or serious adverse events in healthy adults. Gastrointestinal tolerability defined the practical single-dose ceiling. These findings establish the first human safety and pharmacokinetic profile of a novel, orally administered actinide chelator and support further clinical evaluation of HOPO 14-1 as a countermeasure for internal radionuclide and heavy metal contamination. Development of a deployable and population-level emergency intervention addresses a long-standing unmet need with important implications for public health preparedness. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05628961.

title: Safety and Efficacy of Apixaban Therapy for Coronary Artery Aneurysms After Kawasaki Disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Anticoagulation combined with aspirin lowers the risk of coronary thrombosis in patients with large/giant coronary artery aneurysms following Kawasaki disease. We aimed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of apixaban in this high-risk pediatric population and compare it to conventional anticoagulant therapy. METHODS: In this retrospective study, we described our experience with the use of apixaban in patients with Kawasaki disease with large/giant coronary artery aneurysms. In patients who were previously exposed to conventional anticoagulation, we compared rates of new coronary thrombosis or myocardial infarction (effectiveness) and clinically relevant bleeding (safety) during apixaban versus antecedent conventional therapy. All patients received concomitant antiplatelet agents. Apixaban dosing was guided by weight and anti-Xa chromogenic assays. RESULTS: Between 2018 and 2025, 28 patients with Kawasaki disease (median age 6.7 years; 75% male) with large/giant coronary artery aneurysms were prescribed apixaban. Of these, 27 (96%) had previously received vitamin K antagonists or low molecular weight heparin. The rates of new coronary thrombosis and new myocardial infarctions were not higher when patients received apixaban versus conventional anticoagulation (0.025 versus 0.041 events per person-year; incidence rate ratio [IRR], 0.61 [95% CI, 0.06-3.3] and 0.013 versus 0.041 events per person-year; IRR, 0.31 [95% CI, 0.01-2.5], respectively). Rates of clinically relevant bleeding were also not higher for apixaban versus conventional therapy (0.038 versus 0.058 events per person-year, IRR, 0.66 [95% CI, 0.11-2.5]). CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective single-center series of pediatric patients with Kawasaki disease with large/giant coronary artery aneurysms, apixaban combined with antiplatelet therapy was well tolerated and demonstrated no evidence of increased harm relative to conventional anticoagulants. Multicenter research is needed to confirm these findings and define the optimal therapeutic range for apixaban in this high-risk population.

title: Anticoagulation in Subclinical Atrial Fibrillation: An Evidence-Based Framework for Individualized Management.
abstract: The increasing use of wearable monitoring technologies and cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) has led to frequent incidental detection of subclinical atrial fibrillation (SCAF), yet the role of long-term anticoagulation remains uncertain. Growing evidence indicates that SCAF is a separate clinical entity on the continuous spectrum of atrial disease and not just a precursor to clinical disease. We propose that anticoagulation in SCAF should be guided by integrating arrythmia burden, baseline clinical risk and the degree of structural atrial cardiomyopathy in addition to life expectancy and patient preferences. This review synthesizes data from observational studies, randomized clinical trials, and post-hoc analyses to provide a comprehensive and practical framework for individualized anticoagulation, and risk-benefit considerations.

title: Acute aortic syndrome rule-out criteria: development and external validation.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Acute aortic syndrome (AAS) is a rare but catastrophic event, presenting with non-specific symptoms that mimic common conditions, and carries a mortality approaching 80% when missed. Current clinical tools, including the Aortic Dissection Detection Risk Score (ADD-RS) and its refinement, the simplified AORTA score, achieve high sensitivity when combined with D-dimer but fail to identify a population at sufficiently low risk to safely avoid further testing. To address this gap, the Acute Aortic Syndrome Rule-Out Criteria (ARC) were developed and validated, a pragmatic bedside tool designed to safely exclude AAS in low-risk patients without additional testing. METHODS: A retrospective multistep derivation and validation study was conducted. The derivation cohort included patients with confirmed AAS from the International Registry of Acute Aortic Dissection (IRAD). Starting from existing scores, candidate predictors were identified from the IRAD dataset and sequentially added to achieve sensitivity ≥ 99%. External validation was performed in patients with suspected AAS across three prospective multicentre cohorts (ADvISED, PROFUNDUS, and DAShED). Diagnostic accuracy was assessed using sensitivity and specificity with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: The final seven-variable ARC included age >60 years, abrupt onset pain, severe pain, hypotension/shock, neurological deficit, pulse deficit, and known aortic disease. Patients were classified as positive if any ARC variable was present and negative only if all variables were absent. In the derivation cohort, ARC achieved a sensitivity of 99.2% (95% CI 99.1-99.3). In the ADvISED/PROFUNDUS cohort (4598 patients, 10.2% AAS prevalence), sensitivity was 100% (95% CI 99.2-100) with specificity 23.7% (95% CI 22.4-25.0). In the DAShED cohort (5346 patients, 0.3% prevalence), sensitivity was 100% (95% CI 76.8-100) and specificity 36.4% (95% CI 35.1-37.7), ruling out 36.3% of patients without missing any AAS cases. CONCLUSIONS: ARC is an externally validated, pragmatic clinical rule demonstrating high diagnostic sensitivity in a large external validation cohort. When incorporated into existing diagnostic pathways, ARC has the potential to reduce unnecessary testing while maintaining diagnostic performance. Further prospective validation is required to confirm its clinical utility.

title: Effects of Exercise Preconditioning on Promoting Endogenous Recovery Responses After Ischemic Stroke in Late-Adult Mice.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke causes substantial neurological impairment, and although poststroke rehabilitation can support recovery, neurological deficits often limit the feasibility of exercise in clinical settings. Prestroke exercise has emerged as a potential strategy to enhance resilience to ischemic injury, but most preclinical studies have relied on young adult rodents, in which spontaneous recovery can sometimes obscure clinically meaningful functional effects. However, the impact of exercise preconditioning in later stages of adulthood remains insufficiently characterized. Here, we investigated whether a treadmill exercise preconditioning regimen confers neuroprotection and improves recovery-related responses in late-adult mice subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion. METHODS: Eight-month-old male mice were assigned to sedentary or exercise groups. Following 5 weeks of treadmill running (5 days per week after 1 week of acclimatization), mice underwent 45 minutes of middle cerebral artery occlusion and reperfusion. Behavioral assessments and body-weight monitoring were performed before and after middle cerebral artery occlusion. Infarct volume and cellular responses were evaluated 14 days after stroke. RESULTS: Fourteen days after stroke, lesion volume was significantly reduced in the exercise group compared with sedentary controls. Exercise preconditioning enhanced neurogenesis, oligodendrogenesis, and CD31-positive vascular responses while suppressing reactive astrocyte activation. Functional improvements were consistently observed across multiple behavioral assays in late-adult mice. CONCLUSIONS: Preconditioning with treadmill exercise provides neuroprotection against ischemic stroke in late-adult mice by reducing infarct volume and promoting recovery-associated cellular responses. These findings demonstrate that the functional benefits of prestroke exercise extend beyond the young adult stage and support the potential value of regular physical activity as a strategy to mitigate ischemic brain injury later in adulthood.

title: Right Heart Dysfunction in Valvular Heart Disease: Epidemiology, Prognosis, and Management Considerations.
abstract: Right ventricular (RV) dysfunction is an important determinant of clinical outcomes across a wide range of cardiovascular pathologies. As the prevalence of valvular heart disease (VHD) increases with the aging population, the intersection between RV function and VHD will become all the more relevant for proper risk assessment, treatment selection, and prognostication. Even though RV dysfunction may not always be attributed to VHD, we aim to give clinicians, researchers, and regulators a deep understanding of how patients with VHD should be evaluated for RV dysfunction and treated when RV dysfunction coexists with VHD. We begin with a discussion of the epidemiology and diagnostic evaluation of RV dysfunction in patients with a variety of VHD subgroups, including right-side (ie, associated with the tricuspid valve) and left-side (ie, associated with the mitral and aortic valves) VHD. Attention is also given in that section to contemporary methods and evolving techniques for identifying and phenotyping different forms of RV dysfunction in patients with VHD. No single imaging test practically or comprehensively captures all degrees and forms of RV dysfunction in patients with VHD; therefore, the discussion emphasizes integrating evidence from different imaging modalities and hemodynamic assessments. The second component of the review discusses how RV dysfunction affects therapeutic options, including medical, transcatheter, and surgical therapies for VHD. The focus of the discussion is on the interplay between RV dysfunction in patients with right-side VHD, namely tricuspid regurgitation (TR). Unlike left-side VHD, where RV dysfunction is a marker of overall disease severity but does not necessarily indicate futility or nonresponse to therapy, right-side VHD and TR-associated RV dysfunction identifies a subset of patients where intervention may precipitate even worse RV function. The nuances of these interactions between ventricular and valvular function are the emphasis of this section, and we aim to provide a framework for understanding RV function in the context of these different forms of VHD. Finally, the review concludes with an eye to the future, discussing the ways in which RV dysfunction can be identified and managed with the use of novel techniques. This discussion is increasingly relevant as RV dysfunction and VHD frequently coexist, and accurate identification is critical to matching the right treatment for the right patient.

title: Associations of Cumulative Wrist Accelerometer-Derived Physical Activity and Proxies of Sedentary Behavior With Early Cardiac Remodeling in Healthy Adolescents.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Physical inactivity and sedentary behavior are associated with adverse cardiac remodeling in adults, but evidence in adolescence remains limited. This study examined associations of cumulative accelerometer-derived physical activity and proxies of sedentary behavior during adolescence with early subclinical cardiac features assessed by cardiovascular magnetic resonance. METHODS: A total of 111 adolescents (55.9% girls) wore a wrist-worn triaxial accelerometer at ages 12, 14, and 16 years to measure physical activity and sedentary behavior proxies. A 3-Tesla cardiovascular magnetic resonance scan was performed at final follow-up to assess cardiac structure and function. Multivariable linear regression models examined associations between cumulative physical activity and sedentary behavior proxies and cardiovascular magnetic resonance-derived metrics. RESULTS: Daily step counts were positively associated with indexed end-diastolic and end-systolic volumes of the left ventricle (adjusted β per 1000 steps/d, 0.90 mL/m2.7 [95% CI, 0.42-1.37]; 0.36 mL/m2.7 [95% CI, 0.10-0.63], respectively) and the right ventricle (adjusted β per 1000 steps/d, 1.03 mL/m2.7 [95% CI, 0.44-1.61]; 0.44 mL/m2.7 [95% CI, 0.05-0.82], respectively), and with reduced right ventricular longitudinal strain (adjusted β per 1000 steps/d, 0.53% [95% CI, 0.16-0.91]). Greater time spent in sedentary bouts and a higher number of sedentary bouts were associated with increased left atrial active emptying fraction (adjusted β per 100 min/d, 8.21% [95% CI, 0.09-16.34]; adjusted β per 1 bout/d, 1.76% [95% CI, 0.17-3.35], respectively). CONCLUSIONS: Physical inactivity and sedentary behavior proxies during adolescence were independently associated with early markers of ventricular and atrial remodeling. These findings highlight early cardiac adaptations related to lifestyle behaviors and underscore the importance of promoting active lifestyles from a young age.

title: Longitudinal Inflammatory Trajectories and Recurrent Vascular Events After Acute Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Inflammation contributes to the pathophysiology of acute ischemic stroke, yet no inflammatory biomarker has been established as a standard prognostic tool. Most prior studies have relied on single baseline measurements, and the prognostic relevance of longitudinal inflammatory changes remains uncertain. We investigated whether baseline levels and longitudinal trajectories of inflammatory burden index (IBI) and hs-CRP (high-sensitivity C-reactive protein) are associated with recurrent stroke and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, 374 patients with acute ischemic stroke were analyzed. IBI was calculated as hs-CRP multiplied by the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio. Serum hs-CRP and leukocyte differentials were measured within 24 hours of admission and at 6 months (±3 months). Baseline hs-CRP was dichotomized at 2 mg/L and IBI at the median baseline value (4.03 mg/L), and longitudinal trajectories were defined as persistent low, increased, decreased, or persistent high based on changes between baseline and follow-up measurements. RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 30.5 months, 58 patients (15.5%) experienced recurrent stroke and 69 (18.4%) experienced MACE. Baseline IBI and hs-CRP showed inconsistent associations with these outcomes. In contrast, persistent high IBI was associated with increased risks of recurrent stroke (hazard ratio [HR] 2.46; 95% CI, 1.26-4.78; P=0.008) and MACE (HR 2.42; 95% CI, 1.33-4.43; P=0.004) compared with persistent low IBI. Persistent high hs-CRP was associated with MACE (HR 1.92; 95% CI, 1.08-3.41; P=0.026) but not with recurrent stroke. CONCLUSIONS: Persistent high IBI trajectories were independently associated with recurrent stroke and MACE, and persistent high hs-CRP trajectories were associated with MACE. Longitudinal assessment of inflammatory biomarkers may provide prognostic information beyond a single baseline measurement after ischemic stroke.

title: Assessment of Coronary Inflammatory Risk From Noncontrast Cardiac Computed Tomography.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Individuals with low or minimal coronary artery calcification (CAC) are considered at low cardiovascular risk, but a substantial absolute number of cardiovascular events occur in this population; assessment of coronary inflammation using the fat attenuation index (FAI) score may identify residual inflammatory risk beyond CAC score. OBJECTIVE: To assess whether coronary inflammation measured on coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) or noncontrast cardiac CT (NCCT) identifies individuals at high cardiovascular risk independent of CAC burden. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: In this cohort study, a novel artificial intelligence algorithm for measuring FAI score on NCCT was trained and tested in an independent, multicenter, longitudinal cohort of consecutive individuals undergoing clinically indicated CCTA and NCCT for CAC score between 2010 and 2021, with median (IQR) follow-up of 6.7 (4.6-10.0) years. Data were analyzed from January 2010 to March 2024. EXPOSURE: Agatston CAC score and coronary inflammation from both CCTA (CCTA FAI score, established biomarker) and NCCT (NC FAI score, novel biomarker). MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was cardiovascular (CV) mortality; the secondary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), comprising myocardial infarction, new-onset heart failure, or CV death. RESULTS: The derivation cohort included 6818 individuals (median [IQR] age, 61 [51-71] years; 3543 female participants [52.0%]), and the external validation clinical outcomes cohort included 19 110 individuals (median [IQR] age, 56.0 [48.0-64.0] years; 9289 female participants [48.6%]). During follow-up, 536 CV deaths and 1727 MACE occurred. FAI scores independently stratified CV mortality risk across CAC score categories, with the strongest associations among individuals with CAC score of 0. Adding CCTA FAI score or NC FAI score to CAC score significantly improved risk discrimination (area under the curve increased from 0.76 to 0.81 and 0.80, respectively; P < .001), reclassification (net reclassification index), and net benefit across all risk thresholds. Among 89 CV deaths in individuals with CAC score of 0 and 138 CV deaths with CAC score of 1 through 99, 44.9% and 44.2% had NC FAI score above the 75th percentile, respectively. Among individuals with CAC score of 0, CV mortality rates increased from 1.4 to 4.0 per 1000 person-years for those with NC FAI score above the 75th percentile, and MACE rates increased from 5.9 to 13.3 per 1000 person-years. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Per the results of this cohort study, NC FAI score provides prognostic performance comparable to CCTA FAI score and improves cardiovascular risk prediction and reclassification beyond CAC score. Elevated FAI score, derived from either CCTA or NCCT, should be interpreted as a risk-enhancing factor that may prompt intensification of established, evidence-based preventive measures and may serve as a potential future gatekeeper for the use of targeted anti-inflammatory treatments.
